newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic daily power firms on outage rumour.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic daily power firms on outage rumour.

text.p: Day-ahead prices of bulk electricity in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic market firmed Wednesday on rumours of an unplanned outage at a power facility in Pennsylvania.
The price spike for daily power was mitigated by falling power demand due to a brief warm front moving into the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district, market sources said.
"The load is going down anyway," said a PJM power trader.

According to market sources, a unit at PECO Energy Co's Eddystone, Pa., generating station tripped off line earlier today for unspecified problems. The outage forced PECO to cover its load in the daily spot market, they said.
There are two 300 megawatt (MW) coal-fired units and two 395 MW fuel oil-/natural gas-fired units at Eddystone. PECO does not comment on the operation of its fossil-fired plants.
Separately, PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick nuclear unit 2 is in the process of ramping down toward its scheduled refueling shutdown at the end of the month.
Firm, peak PJM electricity prices for Thursday (excluding transmission costs) climbed to $26.00-$27.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Tuesday's $24.00-$26.00.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Thursday delivery held steady at $13.00-$14.00.
Today's hourly dispatch rate in PJM was last quoted near $29.00 after briefly hitting $80.00 this morning.
February PJM electricity jumped to $28.90-$29.60 from $28.60-$29.00 Tuesday.
March PJM electricity firmed to $24.50-$24.65, higher than Tuesday's $24.10-$24.20.
PJM deliveries April and May narrowed to $22.20-22.40 from Tuesday's $22.00-$22.50.
June power prices in PJM were assessed at $24.90-$25.20, compared with Tuesday's $25.25-$25.50.
July/August PJM deliveries tightened to $30.35-$30.65 from Tuesday's $30.40-$30.80.
The natural gas market continued its recent losses on the mild weather outlook next week.
Swing gas values at the Philadelphia city gate softened to to $2.95-$3.35 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) from Tuesday's $3.40 level.
As of 1303 EST, NYMEX February Henry Hub gas futures fell 2.6 cents at $2.890/mmBtu, erasing an early 8.4 cent gain.
